title: Count Vowels in a String
description: Given a lowercase string s, return how many vowels it contains.
inputFormat: A lowercase string s without spaces
outputFormat: Return the number of vowels in s
intendedApproachSummary: Scan each character once and increment the answer when the character is one of a, e, i, o, or u.
wrongApproachHints: Do not use nested loops for each vowel.
A simple membership check per character is enough.
hints: Look at one character at a time.
Keep a running count of vowels.

examples.explanation: The vowels are e, u, a, i, and o.

title: Reverse a String
description: Given a lowercase string s, return its reversed form.
inputFormat: A lowercase string s without spaces
intendedApproachSummary: Traverse from the back or use stack-like reversal behavior to build the answer in reverse order.
wrongApproachHints: Do not mutate immutable strings repeatedly in a long loop.
Every original character must appear exactly once in the output.
hints: The last character should become the first.
A builder or stack can help collect characters.

examples.explanation: The characters appear in reverse order.

title: Check Palindrome String
description: Given a lowercase string s, return true if it is a palindrome, otherwise false.
inputFormat: A lowercase string s without spaces
outputFormat: Return true if s is a palindrome, else false
intendedApproachSummary: Compare characters from both ends and move inward until the pointers cross or a mismatch is found.
wrongApproachHints: Move both pointers after a successful comparison.
Stop early when a mismatch is found.
hints: Check the first and last characters first.
If they match, the middle substring has the same problem.

examples.explanation: The string reads the same from both ends.

title: Valid Anagram
description: Given two lowercase strings a and b, return true if b is an anagram of a, otherwise false.
inputFormat: Two lowercase strings a and b without spaces
outputFormat: Return true if they are anagrams, else false
intendedApproachSummary: If lengths differ, return false. Otherwise count characters in both strings and compare the counts.
wrongApproachHints: Sorting works but the intended linear solution uses frequency counting.
Different lengths can never be anagrams.
hints: Count how many times each letter appears.
Two strings are anagrams only if every count matches.

examples.explanation: Both strings contain the same letters with the same frequencies.

functionContract.javaSignature: public boolean isAnagram(String first, String second)

title: Merge Strings Alternately
description: Given two strings word1 and word2, return a new string formed by taking characters alternately from each word, starting with word1.
inputFormat: Two lowercase strings word1 and word2 without spaces
edgeCases: One string longer than the other
intendedApproachSummary: Use two indices and append from each string when its index is still inside bounds.
wrongApproachHints: Do not stop when the shorter string ends.
Keep the alternating order consistent.
hints: Advance one index in word1, then one in word2.
If one word finishes, append the rest of the other word.

examples.explanation: Characters are taken alternately from each word.

functionContract.javaSignature: public String mergeAlternately(String first, String second)

title: Remove Adjacent Duplicates
description: Repeatedly remove adjacent equal characters from a string until no such pair remains, then return the final string.
inputFormat: A lowercase string s without spaces
outputFormat: Return the reduced string, or Empty if nothing remains
intendedApproachSummary: Use a stack-like builder: if the next character matches the current top, remove the top; otherwise push the new character.
wrongApproachHints: Repeated substring deletion is slower than the intended stack-like simulation.
A removal can create a new adjacent pair.
hints: Think of the answer prefix as a stack.
Compare the new character with the last kept character.

examples.explanation: bb is removed first, then aa is removed.

title: Backspace String Compare
description: Given two strings s and t where # means backspace, return true if both strings are equal after applying the backspaces.
inputFormat: Two strings s and t without spaces
outputFormat: Return true if both become equal, else false
intendedApproachSummary: Process both strings with stack-like behavior, then compare the resulting cleaned strings.
wrongApproachHints: Do not pop from an empty simulated stack.
Apply backspaces to both strings before comparing.
hints: Build a helper that simulates typing with backspaces.
Two cleaned strings must match exactly.

functionContract.javaSignature: public boolean backspaceCompare(String first, String second)

title: Reverse Words in a Sentence
description: Given a sentence that may contain leading, trailing, or multiple spaces between words, return the sentence with the word order reversed and single spaces between words.
inputFormat: A full line string s that may contain spaces
outputFormat: Return the reversed-word sentence with clean spacing
intendedApproachSummary: Parse words while ignoring extra spaces, collect them, then rebuild the sentence from the last word to the first with single spaces.
wrongApproachHints: Do not keep empty words created by repeated spaces.
The final output should not start or end with spaces.
hints: Trim conceptual empty gaps while scanning.
Rebuild with exactly one space between chosen words.

examples.explanation: Extra spaces are removed and the word order is reversed.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
description: Given a lowercase string s, return the length of the longest substring with all distinct characters.
inputFormat: A lowercase string s without spaces
outputFormat: Return the maximum valid substring length
edgeCases: Duplicate reappears after a long gap
intendedApproachSummary: Use a sliding window with character counts or last-seen positions. Shrink the left side when the current character would create a duplicate.
wrongApproachHints: Do not restart the scan from every index.
The window must be adjusted when duplicates appear.
hints: Track which characters are currently inside the window.
Update the best length after the window becomes valid.

examples.explanation: abc is the longest substring with all distinct characters.

title: Longest Common Subsequence
description: Given two strings a and b, return the length of their longest common subsequence.
inputFormat: Two strings a and b without spaces
edgeCases: One string empty after conceptual trimming is not allowed here
One string fully appears as a subsequence in the other
intendedApproachSummary: Build a 2D DP table over prefixes of both strings. Matching characters extend the diagonal answer; otherwise take the best from top or left.
wrongApproachHints: Substring and subsequence are different.
Greedy matching from left to right is not enough.
hints: Define dp[i][j] for the first i characters of a and first j of b.
What happens when the current characters match?

examples.explanation: ace is a common subsequence of length 3.

functionContract.javaSignature: public int lcsLength(String a, String b)

title: Edit Distance
description: Given two strings word1 and word2, return the minimum number of insertions, deletions, and replacements needed to convert word1 into word2.
inputFormat: Two strings word1 and word2 without spaces
intendedApproachSummary: Use DP on prefixes. Matching characters copy the diagonal value; otherwise take one plus the minimum of insert, delete, and replace transitions.
wrongApproachHints: Do not confuse insert/delete directions in the DP table.
A local greedy replacement is not always globally optimal.
hints: What should dp[i][0] and dp[0][j] mean?
When characters differ, try all three edit operations conceptually.

examples.explanation: horse -> rorse -> rose -> ros takes three edits.

functionContract.javaSignature: public int editDistance(String word1, String word2)
